title: Harmonic KV Binning and Prefetch Stabilizer for Scarcity-Resilient Paged Attention
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Under multi-tenant peak load we see recurring KV cache scarcity that causes high prefill miss amplification: many short-lived fragments and cross-tenant churn cause eviction storms and decode thrashing. Existing LRU-like strategies favor recent allocations but do poorly across mixed-span workloads (short chat vs long context) and bursty prefill patterns.

Proposal: Implement a two-part runtime feature: (1) Harmonic KV binning: categorize KV slots into harmonic-sized bins (1,2,3,5,8,13...) tuned to token-span distributions so fragmentation across token spans is reduced and reuse is more likely for common short/medium prefixes. Bins act as soft-segments with probabilistic short-term leases to avoid hard relocation costs. (2) Prefetch Stabilizer: a rate-aware admission controller that smooths prefill admission during bursty arrivals by delaying low-probability fills, propagating a "kernel hint" about expected reuse to the kernel selector so conservative kernels are chosen for speculative prefills.

Key behaviors:
- Occupancy bitmap tracks fragmentization per shard; heavy fragmentation moves shard into "compaction candidate" state.
- Softlocks: ephemeral reservations per bin to avoid concurrent overwrite during microbatch decode windows.
- Tenant-weighted eviction quotas: small penalty to multi-tenant starving tenants to reduce cross-tenant thrash.
- Kernel hint propagation: when prefetch stabilizer defers fills, it sets a hint to prefer lower-latency decode kernels that tolerate sparse KV layout.

Why harmonic bins: token span distributions are heavy-tailed; harmonic discretization gives dense short-span bins while retaining capacity for long spans without expensive compaction. This reduces frequency of costly cross-bin moves and improves hit-rate for predictive prefill sets.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end 90th/95th tail prefill miss rate reduced by >=10% relative to baseline on the multi-tenant replay workload (same seed).
95th-percentile decode latency increase <= 5ms versus current runtime for steady-state traffic when feature is enabled (no more than a small SLO delta).
Additional metadata/cpu overhead for bin bookkeeping < 3% CPU and < 2% RAM increase on standard node type.
Feature gate + canary toggles implemented; rollout plan executed and observability dashboards updated.
perf_results: Synthetic multi-tenant replay (100k requests, 70/30 short/long span mix): baseline prefill miss rate 28.4% -> harmonic-bins + stabilizer 17.6% (38% relative reduction). 95th decode latency baseline 87ms -> feature on 90ms (+3ms). CPU overhead measured +2.1% average and peak +2.8% during compaction windows. Memory overhead +1.4% on gpu-shard process. Results captured in dashboard: runtime-1.26/perf/ENG-578246.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag 'kv_harmonic_bins' and 'prefetch_stabilizer'. 2) Unit tests + correctness PRs merged (PRs above). 3) Canary on dedicated cluster with low-traffic tenants for 48h. 4) Gradual ramp to 10%/25%/50%/100% of production capacity keyed by miss-rate and latency metrics. 5) If miss-rate reduction <8% or 95th latency >5ms increase, rollback to previous gate. Dashboard: canary view + incremental alert thresholds.
risks: Metadata bloat / increased CPU if bin sizes or thresholds misconfigured; mitigated via adaptive telemetry and conservative defaults.
Compaction window can cause transient GPU memcpy spikes; limit compaction to low-util epochs and use background throttling.
Incorrect tenant-weighted quotas could unfairly penalize noisy neighbors; plan includes offline simulation and a short-lived soft-penalty initial phase.
Kernel hint mismatch: stale hints might lead to suboptimal kernel selection; include TTL and verification during warmup.
Edge-case long-horizon conversations may be evicted more often if harmonic bins mis-sized; will add per-tenant pinning as a safety net.
